title: Erasure preserves runs outside the path
statement:
Let $s$ have a subprotocol path into $r$, and fix inputs $x\in X$ and $y\in Y$. Let $P$ be a family of protocols indexed by bits with $P(b)=r$, and let $N$ be a protocol constructor on such families. Fix a bit $c$ such that for every family $Q$, running $N(Q)$ on $(x,y)$ gives the same output as running $Q(c)$ on $(x,y)$. Let $Q$ be a family satisfying $Q(b)=E$ and $Q(

replaced:
Let $s$ be a subprotocol of $r$ via a subprotocol path $h_s$, let $(x,y)$ be an input
pair, and let $N$ be a node constructor (an Alice or Bob node) such that for every
family $Q$ of children, running $N(Q)$ on $(x,y)$ is the same as running $Q(c)$ on $(x,y)$
for a fixed bit $c$. Let $P$ be a family of children with $P(b) = r$, and let $Q$ be the
family obtained from $P$ by replacing the branch $b$ by the erasure of $h_s$ while keeping
the sibling $Q(\neg b) = P(\neg b)$. Assume that if $(x,y)$ reaches $s$ along the path
then $c \ne b$, and that (inductively) if $(x,y)$ does not reach $s$ along the path then
the erasure of $h_s$ runs like $r$ on $(x,y)$. Then $N(Q)$ and $N(P)$ produce the same
output on $(x,y)$.
